tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

## pencil
This MCP server is for interacting with pen.dev apps and .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via the MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Make sure you are aware of the .pen schema and the instructions for the execute tool.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

---

## 1. Corpus MM3-H — discipline d'accès
### G. Handles (instance `HandlePool`, §4)

| ID | Scénario | Attendu | Source | Classe |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H30 | Résolution d'un handle après libération puis réutilisation de son entrée | `fail` | §4, génération | Lib |
| H31a | Deux `resolve Modify` simultanés, quels que soient les handles | le second : `reject` | §4, exclusivité de la valeur pool | Lib |
| H31b | `resolveMany Modify` de deux handles désignant la même entrée | `fail` | §4, distinction dynamique | Lib |
| H32 | `freeSlot` pendant qu'un accès résolu sur l'entrée est actif | `reject` | §4, O3.2 | Lib |
| H33 | Accès résolu rangé dans une valeur d'un cadre plus ancien que le pool | `reject` | G4 | Lib |
| H34 | Un handle copié dans deux structures, résolutions `Modify` successives | `ok` | §4 | Lib |
| H34b | Handle d'un autre pool | `fail` | §4, identité du pool | Lib |
| H44 | Graphe cyclique dont les nœuds vivent dans un pool posé sur un bloc d'arène, liens par handles ; résolutions temporaires ; fin des résolutions puis de la valeur pool, puis `reset` de l'arène, sans parcourir les liens cycliques | `ok` | §4, A10 | Lib |

### H. Rejets abusifs (le modèle doit accepter)

| ID | Scénario | Attendu | Source | Classe | Couvert |
## 4. Contrat du pool de handles (instance de bibliothèque, comme l'arène)

**Principe.** Un handle est une donnée ; il ne porte aucune autorité. La résolution fournit un accès temporaire de seconde classe. Aucun drapeau d'emprunt par entrée : l'exclusivité d'une résolution `Modify` découle des règles du noyau (I1, O3.2), par la forme de l'arbre de dérivation ci-dessous.

**État de l'entrée de pool** (abstrait, comme l'entrée d'arène ; sa représentation en octets est une obligation de l'implémentation) : `{id, storage, internal, slots}`.
- `id` : identité de pool fraîche à chaque `newPool`, jamais réutilisée pendant l'exécution. Un pool détruit puis recréé, même sur le même stockage, a une autre identité.
- `slots` : chaque entrée est `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}` ; `place` est une partie de `storage`.
- La valeur pool est le détenteur de `internal` (même règle que F1). Le stockage peut être local, statique, alloué ou un bloc.

**Handle** : `(id, slot, gen)`, une donnée de taille fixe.

**Emprunt composé.** Une résolution est un emprunt composé : une autorité **compagne** dérivée de `internal` sur **tout le stockage** du pool, au mode de la résolution, détenue par le cadre courant ; puis une autorité d'**entrée** par handle résolu, dérivée **de la compagne** (sous-empreinte), au même mode, détenue par le cadre courant et étiquetée de la génération résolue. Conséquences, toutes par les règles existantes du noyau :
- la compagne ne peut être libérée tant qu'une de ses autorités d'entrée est active (O3.2) ;
- une compagne `Modify` active rend le mode effectif de `internal` absent sur tout le stockage : toute nouvelle résolution, `Modify` ou `Observe`, est rejetée, quels que soient les handles ;
- plusieurs compagnes `Observe` coexistent ; une résolution `Modify` est alors rejetée.

**Opérations**

- **`newPool storage internal`** : préconditions de `newArena` (F1, F2, J1) ; identité fraîche ; toutes les entrées libres, générations à 0.
- **`allocSlot pool dst : ok | fail | reject`** : droit de mise à jour sur la valeur pool (`Modify` exerçable ou `writeShared` sur métadonnées `SharedMutable`) ; `dst` est une feuille non `Init`, ne détenant aucune autorité active, de la taille d'un handle, `Modify` exerçable ; `fail` si aucune entrée libre (état inchangé) ; `ok` : une entrée libre devient vivante, son contenu reste `Uninit`, le handle `(id, slot, gen)` est écrit dans `dst`, qui seule passe à `Init`.
- **`resolve h m : ok | fail | reject`** (`m` = `Observe` ou `Modify`) : droit d'exercice de `internal` au mode `m` par la valeur pool ; les vérifications d'identité et de génération lisent seulement les métadonnées et précèdent toute création d'autorité ; `fail` (état inchangé) si `h.id` n'est pas l'identité du pool, si `h.gen` diffère de la génération de l'entrée, ou si l'entrée est libre ; `ok` : emprunt composé à une entrée. Une compagne déjà active n'est jamais réutilisée : chaque résolution crée la sienne.
- **`resolveMany hs m : ok | fail | reject`** : une compagne, une autorité d'entrée par handle (par `split` de la compagne) ; `fail` si un handle est périmé ou d'un autre pool, ou si deux handles désignent la même entrée ; **atomique** : en cas de `fail`, aucune autorité n'est créée. Coût dynamique explicite : vérification de distinction proportionnelle au lot. C'est la voie des requêtes ECS.
- **`unresolve`** : `release` des autorités d'entrée, puis de la compagne.
- **`freeSlot h : ok | fail | reject`** : droit de mise à jour sur la valeur pool ; `fail` si `h` est périmé ou d'un autre pool ; `reject` si une autorité active dérivée de `internal` couvre l'entrée (donc pendant toute résolution du pool, puisque chaque compagne couvre tout le stockage) ; sinon fin logique du contenu de l'entrée **selon `endUse`** (mêmes préconditions : aucune dépendance utilisable, aucune feuille épinglée ; mêmes effets : feuilles `Uninit`, autorités détenues libérées, dépendances supprimées, stockage possédé logiquement mort, sans désallocation) — `reject` si une précondition d'`endUse` échoue ; une entrée déjà `Uninit` est acceptée ; puis l'entrée devient libre et sa génération est incrémentée.

**Invariant `PoolInv`** (tout pool vivant) : entrées deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; toute autorité active dérivée d'une compagne du pool sur une entrée porte la génération courante de l'entrée, et l'entrée est vivante ; toute compagne active a au plus les autorités d'entrée de sa résolution pour descendants.

**Générations et identités** : `Nat` dans le modèle ; le débordement des générations et l'unicité réelle des identités de pool sont des obligations de l'implémentation, classées bibliothèque et spec 11.

**Théorèmes attendus**
- `pool_resolve_stale_fails`, `pool_resolve_other_pool_fails` ;
- `pool_no_stale_access` : aucune autorité active d'une génération périmée ;
- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` : sur tout état atteint, au plus une compagne `Modify` active par pool, et alors aucune compagne `Observe` — quelle que soit la séquence de `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `release`, `store`, `transfer` et `unresolve` qui y mène ;
- `pool_resolveMany_atomic` et `pool_resolveMany_distinct` ;
- `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` : après `freeSlot`, le contenu de l'entrée satisfait les effets d'`endUse` ;
- `pool_inv_preserved`, et intégration à `Reachable` dans un module séparé, noyau inchangé.

**Cas** : H30–H34b, H44, W1.

## 5. Décision `NoLock` — cadrage

1	import Ern.MM03
2	
3	/-!
4	# Handle pool (jalon 3, step 1)
5	
6	A library instance of the access discipline, like the arena (MM-03.3 §6): the handle pool of the
7	jalon-3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md` v2, §4). A handle is data and carries no authority. A
8	resolution is a compound borrow made of kernel operations of `Ern.MM03`, which this module does
9	not modify: a companion derived from `internal` on the whole storage, then one entry authority per
10	resolved handle, derived from the companion (`derive` for `resolve`, `split` for `resolveMany`).
11	`unresolve` is a sequence of `release`, `freeSlot` an `endUse` of the entry content, `allocSlot` a
12	`write3` of the handle into its destination. The pool entries live beside the kernel state, like
13	the arena entries of MM-03.3.8 but outside `S3`, so the kernel is unchanged.
14	
15	`PReach` extends `Reachable` (MM-03.3 §10) with the pool operations; every pool step is a chain of
16	kernel steps (`pReach_reachable`). Representation choices that the material does not fix are listed
17	in the jalon-3 report, (f).
18	-/
19	
20	namespace Ern.HandlePool
21	
22	open Ern.MM03
23	
24	/-! ## State (material §4) -/
25	
26	/-- Entry of a pool (material §4: `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`): `place` is a part of the
27	pool storage. -/
28	structure Slot where
29	  place : Nat
30	  gen : Nat
31	  live : Bool
32	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
33	
34	/-- Pool entry (material §4: `{id, storage, internal, slots}`), abstract like the arena entry of
35	MM-03.3.8. The pool value is not a field: it is the place that holds `internal` (material §4,
36	"même règle que F1"). -/
37	structure Pool where
38	  id : Nat
39	  storage : Nat
40	  internal : Nat
41	  slots : List Slot
42	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
43	
44	/-- Handle (material §4: `(id, slot, gen)`): data of fixed size, no authority. -/
45	structure Handle where
46	  id : Nat
47	  slot : Nat
48	  gen : Nat
49	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
50	
51	/-- Ghost record of a resolution (material §4, compound borrow): identity and `internal` of the
52	pool, the companion, the mode, and the entry authorities, each tagged with its slot and the
53	resolved generation ("étiquetée de la génération résolue"). Read by no operation except
54	`unresolve`, which looks up the entries of a companion. -/
55	structure Res where
56	  pool : Nat
57	  internal : Nat
58	  comp : Nat
59	  mode : Mode
60	  entries : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)
61	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
62	
63	/-- Kernel state with the pool entries (material §4), the next fresh pool identity ("jamais
64	réutilisée pendant l'exécution") and the ghost record of resolutions. -/
65	structure PS where
66	  s : S3
67	  pools : List Pool
68	  nId : Nat
69	  res : List Res
70	
71	/-- Outcomes of a pool operation (material §4: `ok | fail | reject`): `fail` is a defined failure
72	that leaves the state unchanged, as for `alloc` and `issue` (MM-03.3 §3.1). -/
73	inductive POutcome where
74	  | ok (ps : PS)
75	  | fail (ps : PS)
76	  | reject
77	
78	/-- The pool read as an arena entry with nothing available or issued, to reuse the metadata right
79	and the arena invariant of MM-03.3 §6 (`MetaRight`, `ArenaInv`). -/
80	def Pool.asArena (pl : Pool) : Arena := ⟨pl.storage, pl.internal, [], []⟩
81	
82	/-- Right to update the pool value (material §4, `allocSlot` and `freeSlot`: "`Modify` exerçable
83	ou `writeShared` sur métadonnées `SharedMutable`"): the metadata right of the arena (MM-03.3 §6,
84	`MetaRight`), read on the holder of `internal`. -/
85	def PoolRight (k : K) (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (via : Nat) : Prop := MetaRight k s pl.asArena via
86	
87	instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (via : Nat) :
88	    Decidable (PoolRight k s pl via) := by
89	  unfold PoolRight; infer_instance
90	
91	/-- Place of slot `i` (0 if the slot does not exist). -/
92	def slotPlace (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((pl.slots[i]?).map (·.place)).getD 0
93	
94	/-- The pool with its slot `i` replaced. -/
95	def setSlot (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : Pool := { pl with slots := pl.slots.set i sl }
96	
97	/-- The extended state with its pool `j` replaced. -/
98	def setPool (ps : PS) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) : PS := { ps with pools := ps.pools.set j pl }
99	
100	/-! ## `newPool storage internal` (material §4) -/
101	
102	/-- Preconditions of `newPool storage internal` (material §4: "préconditions de `newArena` (F1, F2,
103	J1)"): those of `newArena` (MM-03.3 §6, O17), read literally, so clause 4 speaks of the arenas of
104	the state. -/
105	def NewPoolPre (s : S3) (storage internal : Nat) : Prop := NewArenaPre s storage internal
106	
107	instance (s : S3) (storage internal : Nat) : Decidable (NewPoolPre s storage internal) := by
108	  unfold NewPoolPre; infer_instance
109	
110	/-- Effect of `newPool storage internal` (material §4): a pool with a fresh identity, one free
111	entry of generation 0 per child of the storage (the entries are the parts of `storage`, report (f)),
112	and the kernel state unchanged. -/
113	def newPoolEff (ps : PS) (storage internal : Nat) : PS :=
114	  { ps with
115	    pools := ps.pools ++ [⟨ps.nId, storage, internal,
116	      (kids ps.s.P storage).map fun q => ⟨q, 0, false⟩⟩]
117	    nId := ps.nId + 1 }
118	
119	/-- `newPool storage internal : ok | reject` as a relation (material §4). -/
120	def NewPoolStep (storage internal : Nat) (ps : PS) : Outcome3 PS → Prop :=
121	  Guarded (NewPoolPre ps.s storage internal) (newPoolEff ps storage internal)
122	
123	/-! ## `allocSlot pool dst` (material §4) -/
124	
125	/-- First free entry of a list of slots, counted from `i`. -/
126	def firstFreeF : Nat → List Slot → Option Nat
127	  | _, [] => none
128	  | i, sl :: l => if sl.live then firstFreeF (i + 1) l else some i
129	
130	/-- First free entry of a pool (report (f): the material does not say which free entry). -/
131	def firstFree (pl : Pool) : Option Nat := firstFreeF 0 pl.slots
132	
133	/-- Static preconditions of `allocSlot pool dst` (material §4): the right to update the pool value;
134	`dst` a usable leaf, not `Init`, holding no active authority, under exercisable `Modify`. The size
135	of a handle is not represented: MM-03 has no sizes (report (f)). -/
136	def AllocSlotStatic (k : K) (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (via dst : Nat) : Prop :=
137	  PoolRight k s pl via ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
138	    s.I dst ≠ .init ∧
139	    ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst)
140	      True
141	
142	instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (via dst : Nat) :
143	    Decidable (AllocSlotStatic k s pl via dst) := by
144	  unfold AllocSlotStatic; infer_instance
145	
146	/-- Effect of `allocSlot` on the entry `i` of the pool `j` (material §4): the entry becomes live,
147	its content stays as it is, the handle is written into `dst`, which alone becomes `Init`. -/
148	def allocSlotEff (ps : PS) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) (dst : Nat) : PS :=
149	  { setPool ps j (setSlot pl i { sl with live := true }) with s := write3Eff ps.s [dst] }
150	
151	/-- The handle written by `allocSlot` into its destination (material §4: `(id, slot, gen)`). -/
152	def slotHandle (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Option Handle :=
153	  (pl.slots[i]?).map fun sl => ⟨pl.id, i, sl.gen⟩
154	
155	/-- `allocSlot pool dst : ok | fail | reject` as a relation (material §4): `reject` when a static
156	precondition fails or the pool does not exist; `fail`, state unchanged, when no entry is free;
157	`ok` otherwise, on the first free entry. -/
158	inductive AllocSlotStep (k : K) (j via dst : Nat) (ps : PS) : POutcome → Prop where
159	  | ok {pl : Pool} {i : Nat} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl →
160	      AllocSlotStatic k ps.s pl via dst → firstFree pl = some i → pl.slots[i]? = some sl →
161	      AllocSlotStep k j via dst ps (.ok (allocSlotEff ps j pl i sl dst))
162	  | fail {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → AllocSlotStatic k ps.s pl via dst →
163	      firstFree pl = none → AllocSlotStep k j via dst ps (.fail ps)
164	  | reject {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AllocSlotStatic k ps.s pl via dst →
165	      AllocSlotStep k j via dst ps .reject
166	  | none : ps.pools[j]? = none → AllocSlotStep k j via dst ps .reject
167	
168	/-! ## `resolve h m` and `resolveMany hs m` (material §4) -/
169	
170	/-- The handle designates a live entry of the pool, at its generation (material §4, `resolve`:
171	`fail` "si `h.id` n'est pas l'identité du pool, si `h.gen` diffère de la génération de l'entrée,
172	ou si l'entrée est libre"). A slot index outside the pool designates no entry (report (f)). -/
173	def HandleOK (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Prop :=
174	  h.id = pl.id ∧ OptP (pl.slots[h.slot]?) (fun sl => sl.gen = h.gen ∧ sl.live = true) False
175	
176	instance (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Decidable (HandleOK pl h) := by
177	  unfold HandleOK; infer_instance
178	
179	/-- Right of the pool value to exercise `internal` at mode `m` (material §4, `resolve`): the
180	precondition of `derive` (MM-03.3 §3, O1) of the companion, from `internal`, on the whole storage.
181	It reads the effective mode of `internal`, so an active `Modify` companion rejects every new
182	resolution, whatever the handles (material §4, H31a). -/
183	def ResolveRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Prop := DerivePre s pl.internal pl.storage m
184	
185	instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Decidable (ResolveRight s pl m) := by
186	  unfold ResolveRight; infer_instance
187	
188	/-- State after the compound borrow of one entry (material §4): the companion `s.A.length`,
189	derived from `internal` on the storage, then the entry authority `s.A.length + 1`, derived from the
190	companion on the place `q` of the entry, both at mode `m`, held by the current frame. -/
191	def resolveS (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
192	  deriveEff (deriveEff s pl.internal pl.storage m) s.A.length q m
193	
194	/-- `resolve h m : ok | fail | reject` on the pool `j` as a relation (material §4): `reject` when
195	the right fails; then `fail`, state unchanged, when the handle is stale, of another pool or names
196	a free entry; `ok` with the compound borrow, recorded with the resolved generation. The derive of
197	the entry is a kernel step: its precondition is checked (`noEntry`). -/
198	inductive ResolveStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (m : Mode) (ps : PS) : POutcome → Prop where
199	  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → HandleOK pl h →
200	      pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
201	      DerivePre (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length sl.place m →
202	      ResolveStep j h m ps (.ok { ps with
203	        s := resolveS ps.s pl sl.place m
204	        res := ps.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, ps.s.A.length, m,
205	          [(ps.s.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] })
206	  | fail {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → ¬ HandleOK pl h →
207	      ResolveStep j h m ps (.fail ps)
208	  | reject {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight ps.s pl m →
209	      ResolveStep j h m ps .reject
210	  | noEntry {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m →
211	      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
212	      ¬ DerivePre (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length sl.place m →
213	      ResolveStep j h m ps .reject
214	  | none : ps.pools[j]? = none → ResolveStep j h m ps .reject
215	
216	/-- The handles of a batch all designate live entries of the pool at their generation, and pairwise
217	distinct entries (material §4, `resolveMany`: `fail` "si un handle est périmé ou d'un autre pool,
218	ou si deux handles désignent la même entrée"). -/
219	def BatchOK (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : Prop :=
220	  (∀ h ∈ hs, HandleOK pl h) ∧ (hs.map (·.slot)).Nodup
221	
222	instance (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : Decidable (BatchOK pl hs) := by
223	  unfold BatchOK; infer_instance
224	
225	/-- Regions of the entries of a batch: the footprint of each designated entry. -/
226	def batchRegions (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : List (List Nat) :=
227	  hs.map fun h => footprint s.P (slotPlace pl h.slot)
228	
229	/-- State after the compound borrow of a batch (material §4): the companion `s.A.length`, then one
230	entry authority per handle by `split` of the companion (MM-03.3 §3, O2). -/
231	def resolveManyS (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
232	  splitEff (deriveEff s pl.internal pl.storage m) s.A.length (batchRegions s pl hs)
233	
234	/-- Entry authorities of a batch with their slot and generation: the `i`-th split authority has the
235	identity `c + 1 + i` for the companion `c`. -/
236	def batchEntries (c : Nat) (hs : List Handle) : List (Nat × Nat × Nat) :=
237	  mapI (fun i h => (i, h.slot, h.gen)) (c + 1) hs
238	
239	/-- `resolveMany hs m : ok | fail | reject` on the pool `j` as a relation (material §4): `reject`
240	when the right fails; then `fail`, state unchanged and no authority created (atomicity), when the
241	batch is not valid; `ok` with the compound borrow when the `split` of the companion is accepted,
242	`reject` otherwise (`noSplit`). -/
243	inductive ResolveManyStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) (ps : PS) :
244	    POutcome → Prop where
245	  | ok {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → BatchOK pl hs →
246	      SplitPre k (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length
247	        (batchRegions ps.s pl hs) →
248	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps (.ok { ps with
249	        s := resolveManyS ps.s pl hs m
250	        res := ps.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, ps.s.A.length, m,
251	          batchEntries ps.s.A.length hs⟩] })
252	  | fail {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → ¬ BatchOK pl hs →
253	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps (.fail ps)
254	  | reject {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight ps.s pl m →
255	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps .reject
256	  | noSplit {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight ps.s pl m → BatchOK pl hs →
257	      ¬ SplitPre k (deriveEff ps.s pl.internal pl.storage m) ps.s.A.length
258	        (batchRegions ps.s pl hs) →
259	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps .reject
260	  | none : ps.pools[j]? = none → ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps .reject
261	
262	/-! ## `unresolve` (material §4) -/
263	
264	/-- Releases the authorities of a list in order (MM-03.3 §3, O3); `none` as soon as a release is
265	rejected. -/
266	def releaseAll : S3 → List Nat → Option S3
267	  | s, [] => some s
268	  | s, a :: l => if ReleasePre s a then releaseAll (releaseEff s a) l else none
269	
270	/-- The resolution whose companion is `c`. -/
271	def findRes (ps : PS) (c : Nat) : Option Res := ps.res.find? fun r => r.comp == c
272	
273	/-- `unresolve` of the resolution of companion `c` as a relation (material §4: "`release` des
274	autorités d'entrée, puis de la compagne"): `ok` when every release is accepted, `reject`
275	otherwise or when `c` is no companion. -/
276	inductive UnresolveStep (c : Nat) (ps : PS) : POutcome → Prop where
277	  | ok {r : Res} {s' : S3} : findRes ps c = some r →
278	      releaseAll ps.s (r.entries.map (·.1) ++ [r.comp]) = some s' →
279	      UnresolveStep c ps (.ok { ps with s := s' })
280	  | reject {r : Res} : findRes ps c = some r →
281	      releaseAll ps.s (r.entries.map (·.1) ++ [r.comp]) = none → UnresolveStep c ps .reject
282	  | none : findRes ps c = none → UnresolveStep c ps .reject

284	/-! ## `freeSlot h` (material §4) -/
285	
286	/-- The handle is current for the pool (material §4, `freeSlot`: `fail` "si `h` est périmé ou d'un
287	autre pool"): same identity, an existing entry of the same generation. -/
288	def HandleCur (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Prop :=
289	  h.id = pl.id ∧ OptP (pl.slots[h.slot]?) (fun sl => sl.gen = h.gen) False
290	
291	instance (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Decidable (HandleCur pl h) := by
292	  unfold HandleCur; infer_instance
293	
294	/-- An active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the place `q` of an entry
295	(material §4, `freeSlot`: `reject` "si une autorité active dérivée de `internal` couvre
296	l'entrée"). -/
297	def EntryBorrowed (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Prop :=
298	  ∃ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j ∧ pl.internal ∈ s.ancs j ∧
299	    ∃ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ footprint s.P q
300	
301	instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (q : Nat) : Decidable (EntryBorrowed s pl q) := by
302	  unfold EntryBorrowed; infer_instance
303	
304	/-- Effect of `freeSlot` on the entry `i` of the pool `j` (material §4): the end of the content of
305	the entry by `endUse` (MM-03.3 §3, O12), then the entry is free and its generation incremented. -/
306	def freeSlotEff (ps : PS) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : PS :=
307	  { setPool ps j (setSlot pl i ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) with
308	    s := endUseEff ps.s sl.place }
309	
310	/-- `freeSlot h : ok | fail | reject` on the pool `j` as a relation (material §4), in order:
311	`reject` without the right to update the pool value; `fail`, state unchanged, for a stale handle
312	or one of another pool; `reject` when an active authority derived from `internal` covers the
313	entry; `reject` when a precondition of `endUse` fails; `ok` otherwise. -/
314	inductive FreeSlotStep (k : K) (j via : Nat) (h : Handle) (ps : PS) : POutcome → Prop where
315	  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → PoolRight k ps.s pl via →
316	      HandleCur pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ EntryBorrowed ps.s pl sl.place →
317	      EndUsePre k ps.s sl.place →
318	      FreeSlotStep k j via h ps (.ok (freeSlotEff ps j pl h.slot sl))
319	  | fail {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → PoolRight k ps.s pl via → ¬ HandleCur pl h →
320	      FreeSlotStep k j via h ps (.fail ps)
321	  | reject {pl : Pool} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ PoolRight k ps.s pl via →
322	      FreeSlotStep k j via h ps .reject
323	  | borrowed {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → PoolRight k ps.s pl via →
324	      HandleCur pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → EntryBorrowed ps.s pl sl.place →
325	      FreeSlotStep k j via h ps .reject
326	  | endUse {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : ps.pools[j]? = some pl → PoolRight k ps.s pl via →
327	      HandleCur pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ EntryBorrowed ps.s pl sl.place →
328	      ¬ EndUsePre k ps.s sl.place → FreeSlotStep k j via h ps .reject
329	  | none : ps.pools[j]? = none → FreeSlotStep k j via h ps .reject

331	/-! ## Reachability extended with the pool (material §4, "intégration à `Reachable`") -/
332	
333	/-- One step of the extended machine: a step of `Reachable` (MM-03.3 §10, `Step`) on the kernel
334	state, or an `ok` pool operation (material §4). -/
335	inductive PStep (k : K) : PS → PS → Prop where
336	  | kernel {ps : PS} {s' : S3} : Step k ps.s s' → PStep k ps { ps with s := s' }
337	  | newPool {ps ps' : PS} {st i : Nat} : NewPoolStep st i ps (.ok ps') → PStep k ps ps'
338	  | allocSlot {ps ps' : PS} {j via dst : Nat} : AllocSlotStep k j via dst ps (.ok ps') →
339	      PStep k ps ps'
340	  | resolve {ps ps' : PS} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} {m : Mode} : ResolveStep j h m ps (.ok ps') →
341	      PStep k ps ps'
342	  | resolveMany {ps ps' : PS} {j : Nat} {hs : List Handle} {m : Mode} :
343	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m ps (.ok ps') → PStep k ps ps'
344	  | unresolve {ps ps' : PS} {c : Nat} : UnresolveStep c ps (.ok ps') → PStep k ps ps'
345	  | freeSlot {ps ps' : PS} {j via : Nat} {h : Handle} : FreeSlotStep k j via h ps (.ok ps') →
346	      PStep k ps ps'

348	/-- Initial extended state: `S3.init statics` (MM-03.3.9), no pool, no resolution. -/
349	def PS.init (statics : Statics) : PS := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0, []⟩
350	
351	/-- States reached from the initial state by kernel, arena and pool steps (material §4, extension of
352	`Reachable`, MM-03.3 §10). -/
353	inductive PReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PS → Prop where
354	  | init : ShapeOK 0 (statics.map (·.1)) → PReach k statics (PS.init statics)
355	  | step {ps ps' : PS} : PReach k statics ps → PStep k ps ps' → PReach k statics ps'
356	
357	/-! ## Kernel steps keep authorities and footprints (MM-03.3 §3–6) -/
358	
359	/-- The authorities of `s` remain in `s'` with their mode and footprint; one active in `s'` was
360	active in `s` and, if it was derived, is still derived. -/
361	def KeepsAuth (s s' : S3) : Prop :=
362	  s.A.length ≤ s'.A.length ∧ ∀ (j : Nat) (y' : Authority), s'.A[j]? = some y' → j < s.A.length →
363	    ∃ y, s.A[j]? = some y ∧ y'.mode = y.mode ∧ y'.footprint = y.footprint ∧
364	      (y'.active = true → y.active = true ∧ (y.origin ≠ none → y'.origin ≠ none))
365	
366	theorem KeepsAuth.refl (s : S3) : KeepsAuth s s :=
367	  ⟨Nat.le_refl _, fun _ y' hy' _ => ⟨y', hy', rfl, rfl, fun ha => ⟨ha, id⟩⟩⟩
368	
369	theorem KeepsAuth.trans {s s₁ s₂ : S3} (h₁ : KeepsAuth s s₁) (h₂ : KeepsAuth s₁ s₂) :
370	    KeepsAuth s s₂ := by
371	  refine ⟨Nat.le_trans h₁.1 h₂.1, fun j y₂ hy₂ hj => ?_⟩
372	  obtain ⟨y₁, hy₁, m₁, f₁, a₁⟩ := h₂.2 j y₂ hy₂ (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le hj h₁.1)
373	  obtain ⟨y, hy, m, f, a⟩ := h₁.2 j y₁ hy₁ hj
374	  exact ⟨y, hy, m₁.trans m, f₁.trans f, fun ha =>
375	    ⟨(a (a₁ ha).1).1, fun ho => (a₁ ha).2 ((a (a₁ ha).1).2 ho)⟩⟩
376	
377	theorem KeepsAuth.of_releases {s s₁ : S3} (h : OnlyReleases s s₁) : KeepsAuth s s₁ :=
378	  ⟨Nat.le_of_eq h.1.symm, fun j z hz _ => by
379	    obtain ⟨y, hy, m, o, f, -, a⟩ := h.2 j z hz
380	    exact ⟨y, hy, m, f, fun ha => ⟨a ha, fun hn => by rw [o]; exact hn⟩⟩⟩
381	
382	theorem KeepsAuth.app {s s₁ : S3} {l : List Authority} (h : s₁.A = s.A ++ l) : KeepsAuth s s₁ :=
383	  ⟨by rw [h]; simp, fun j y' hy' hj => ⟨y', by rw [h, List.getElem?_append_left hj] at hy'; exact hy',
384	    rfl, rfl, fun ha => ⟨ha, id⟩⟩⟩
385	
386	theorem KeepsAuth.same {s s₁ : S3} (h : s₁.A = s.A) : KeepsAuth s s₁ :=
387	  KeepsAuth.app (l := []) (by rw [h, List.append_nil])
388	
389	/-- A kernel step keeps the authorities (MM-03.3 §3–5): it appends, releases, or changes holders;
390	`exitFrame` re-attaches a surviving derived authority to a surviving ancestor (O7, `ExitPre`). -/
391	theorem kstep_keeps {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : KStep k s s') : KeepsAuth s s' := by
392	  cases h with
393	  | derive hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact .app rfl
394	  | split hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact .app rfl
395	  | release hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact .of_releases (release_releases s _)
396	  | transfer hs =>
397	    rename_i src dst
398	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
399	    refine ⟨by simp [transferEff], fun j y' hy' _ => ?_⟩
400	    rw [transfer_A_get] at hy'
